Convert the buyer's request into JSON search filters. Use only the app taxonomy: Furniture (Sofa, Desk, Chair, Dresser), Electronics (Television, Monitor, Speaker), Home Decor (Rug, Lamp), and Appliances (Microwave). Normalize clear synonyms and plurals to these exact names. When a requested item type maps unambiguously to one taxonomy type, output that type and its category. If a recognizable item type is not in the taxonomy but its broad category is clear, output the category, set item_type to null, and preserve the item phrase in q. If only a broad category is stated, do not guess an item type. Preserve useful modifiers not represented by filters in q. Do not infer numeric thresholds from vague terms such as "cheap" or "affordable". Convert explicit price limits to numeric USD min_price/max_price values. Use only these condition values: NEW, LIKE_NEW, GOOD, FAIR, POOR. For fulfillment, include every explicitly acceptable option using PICKUP and/or DELIVERY (for example, if both are acceptable, use ["PICKUP", "DELIVERY"]). Only set bundle or sort when requested; use true/false/null for bundle and newest, price-asc, price-desc, popular, or null for sort. Use arrays for category, item_type, condition, and fulfillment; use null when unspecified. Return JSON only with exactly these fields: q, category, item_type, condition, fulfillment, min_price, max_price, bundle, sort.

Price boundary rules: Treat explicit price ranges as inclusive at both endpoints unless the request uses a strict comparison. For “under $X” or “less than $X,” set max_price to X minus $0.01. For “over $X” or “more than $X,” set min_price to X plus $0.01. For “at most,” “no more than,” “at least,” or “no less than,” include the stated boundary. Interpret “between $X and $Y” as inclusive of both endpoints. Prices are in USD and may use cent precision.
